Q1: A huge city fire. The on-screen text says "1666 — The Great Fire", and the fire spreads for days, from 2 to 7 Sept 1666.
Q2: One small place. It starts in a bakery with an oven fire, labelled "Thomas Farriner, baker to the King". A map highlights a small spot near Pudding Lane and London Bridge. From there it spreads through the packed wooden houses along the river.
Q3: They flee on foot with bundles, carts and wagons piled with belongings. They load their goods into rowing boats and cross the river. They watch the blaze from the water and the far bank. Some camp in open fields with tents and campfires. A bridge also appears crowded with people. Fire-fighting is not clearly shown.
Q4: Not sure. Around frames 49-50 (196-200 s) a large church-like building with a tower sits in the middle of the blaze, and it looks engulfed in flames. The pictures do not clearly show it burning down or being destroyed. A church tower stands amid the ruins in the frames after the fire (frame 69). Whether it is the church on the hill is not certain.
Q5: In brick. A big orange outline shows the burnt area, and the ruins are surveyed. Christopher Wren is shown with a plan, and builders work with bricks and scaffolding. The city is rebuilt with red-brick houses. The new street layout is mostly the old street pattern, not Wren's grand plan: the 1666 plan appears as a small engraved inset, and the 1946 caption reads "same streets" for the second rebuild. One wide new street appears around 1673-77.
Q6: A large white-stone cathedral with a dome appears, shown as a tall building of 365 ft. It is finished around 1710-11 under the caption "The dome rules the skyline". A tall free-standing column appears next to the brick houses (1673-75), labelled 202 ft and shown in an engraving as "The Monument".
Q7: Bombing at night in 1940, captioned "the second great fire" (29-30 Dec 1940). Firefighters hose fires from a muddy riverbank and on rooftops. The city is shown burning, with a counter of 100,000 incendiaries. A large area is outlined in orange. The domed cathedral still stands among the flames and survives. Much of the surrounding city is damaged.
Q8: A modern city of glass and concrete towers and office blocks beside the river, with bridges. The domed cathedral is still visible among the towers. At night the towers' windows glow. A final text card says the film was made from the 1666 survey and old engravings.
